requirements.title: Distinct adoption and artifact qualification

source.excerpt: Policy-2 adoption reports explicitly assess **project adoption**, not release

requirements.rationale: Current qualification and scheduling contract; neither a saved success nor an attributed review is release permission.

criteria.expected: Project adoption never implies an artifact is deliverable; exact digest-bound delivery evidence cannot transfer between stages or bytes.

requirements.title: Bounded review preparation and honest prior-stage observations
requirements.rationale: Current qualification and scheduling contract; neither a saved success nor an attributed review is release permission.

criteria.expected: Review preparation needs no active ledger, never approves itself and keeps prior-stage facts distinct from current execution.

requirements.title: Fail-fast scheduling retains complete qualification obligations

source.excerpt: Required CI uses `check --ci --review-ci --fail-fast`. Review readiness is checked

requirements.rationale: Current qualification and scheduling contract; neither a saved success nor an attributed review is release permission.

criteria.expected: Opt-in fail-fast skips expensive later suites after failure but marks them blocking and unverified; default collection and successful checks still execute once.

review.rationale: Reviewed unchanged adoption scope rejection of nonartifact failures and strengthened artifact preflight assertions. Missing artifact bytes remain distinct from project controls; failed/error/migration and required-standard blockers survive. Completion reporting is stricter but does not rewrite artifact verdicts or authorize release. Rechecked the connected-rehearsal repairs: no policy definitions, consent or runtime gates were weakened. Current-policy bootstrap supplies all four unresolved exact-change controls and preserves them in CLI output; normal GitLab workflow/default wiring and final immutable source-build declarations have new positive and adversarial tests. Existing mapped assertion bodies and scope guards outside these additions are unchanged. Static wiring remains distinct from program trust, live provider access and execution.
